title: Lahpet Thoke
description: Burmese tea leaf salad — soaked green tea leaves pounded into an oily, bitter-bright dressing and mixed at the table with cabbage and a dozen crunchy things.
notes: Fried split peas and crispy garlic are sold ready-made in Asian grocers. Real lahpet is fermented for weeks; the overnight soak here is the home shortcut.

steps.text: Steep the green tea leaves in hot water and drain. Repeat twice more, then cover with cold water and soak overnight to draw out the bitterness.
steps.tip: The repeated steeping is what makes the leaves edible rather than harsh.

steps.text: Squeeze the leaves dry and pound or blend with the garlic, green chilli, lime juice, fish sauce, salt, and peanut oil into a coarse, oily paste.
Arrange the napa cabbage, tomatoes, split peas, peanuts, sesame seeds, fried garlic, and dried shrimp in separate piles around the lahpet.
steps.tip: Served in piles and mixed at the table — the contrast of textures is the point.

steps.text: Mix everything together just before eating, adding more lime juice or fish sauce to taste.
